subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: Should OpenClaw change source-channel delivery so unphased assistant text before or between tool calls is private by default, even when current configs rely on automatic bare-text replies?
rationale: The source-reproducible fix point crosses security, channel delivery, and compatibility: the safest product default may conflict with existing users who depend on automatic visible replies when models do not call the message tool.

options.title: Default-Safe With Migration
options.body: Make inter-tool/unphased assistant text private by default for user-facing channels, keep intentional final replies and message-tool sends, and provide an upgrade/doctor path for deployments relying on automatic bare text.

options.title: Opt-In Strict Mode First
options.body: Keep automatic delivery defaults unchanged and land a documented strict/message-tool-only or final-only mode for affected channels while collecting more live proof.

options.title: PR-by-PR Mitigations
options.body: Continue accepting narrow provider/channel filters without changing the product default, leaving the canonical issue open for remaining leak shapes.

recommendation.title: Default-Safe With Migration
recommendation.body: Make inter-tool/unphased assistant text private by default for user-facing channels, keep intentional final replies and message-tool sends, and provide an upgrade/doctor path for deployments relying on automatic bare text.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision is product/security policy for channel defaults, and steipete is the clearest recent routing signal on the canonical thread.
